messages:
lina: Quick heads-up — I sketched a compact flow for the automatic fallback policy UX. Want to validate assumptions before I wire it into the Console.
mahesh: share the assumptions pls. main worry: surprising route changes and cost spikes.
lina: yep — assumptions are: 1) fallback can be configured per-route, 2) triggers are error-class or latency-based, 3) we show an estimated traffic % and estimated cost delta before enabling.
sam: +1 on visibility. also we need editable trigger windows (eg 5m vs 30s) and hysteresis so it doesn't oscillate.
jess: audit requirements: immutable event id, reason code, pre/post model ids, and sampled request+response for 7 days. We should surface a tiny playback for operators.
mahesh: playback is good but keep it compact. maybe a timeline scrub with markers for trigger events and reason tooltips. :eyes:
rollout-bot: Deploy started: canary policy "autofallback/preview" on infra1 (10% traffic) — id=fb-20260318-07
lina: perfect — can we preview the estimated fallback traffic on that canary? ideally show the projected steady-state vs current.
sam: UX detail: show two toggles — "Preview only (no routing)" and "Apply (routing enabled)". Preview runs sim against recent traffic distribution.
jess: simulation needs to account for quotas/backpressure — we cannot let fallback silently bypass customer quotas. Add a warning modal if projected token usage exceeds quotas.
mahesh: also show an opt-in checkbox: "allow fallback to use dedicated tier" vs "use same tier". That helps cost predictability.
lina: thinking about controls: a compact policy card with: trigger, threshold, window, fallback target, traffic cap, audit sampling rate.
sam: propose the inline policy example in Console UI (compact):
```
trigger: error_rate>5% over 2m
fallback: model-compact-v1
traffic_cap: 30%
audit_sample: 1%
```
jess: sounds good. for audit_sample we should clarify what we store and redact PII by default.
mahesh: question: should operators be able to manually force a fallback (escape hatch) even if policy says no? I think yes, but with an extra confirmation and an automatic expiry.
lina: escape hatch: a temporary override with TTL and an operator reason required — action logged to audit events.
rollout-bot: Canary update: 10% -> 25% after 15m if no triggers. Canary id=fb-20260318-07 status=healthy
sam: minor note — add a small "cost estimate" microcard next to the policy that extrapolates token delta per 100k requests.
jess: I'll draft the audit event schema and playback wireframes. Lina, I'll ping when figma frames are ready.
lina: thanks — I'll prototype the policy card and simulation endpoint contract. tagging follow-ups in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
